And as during the opening phase of the conflict, the US leader’s objectives and methods are clouded in confusion, daily U-turns and boasts that within hours are revealed to be false. Washington’s short-term aim is clear enough – to regain control of the strait of Hormuz from Iran – and the president seems willing to extend the bombing campaign from beyond Iran’s southern shores to achieve this.

Five months of U-turns and false boasts leave Donald Trump in worse position than when he started Donald Trump has taken the war with Iran into a new, murkier phase as the two sides move further and further from the vague memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed on 17 June. And as during the opening phase of the conflict, the US leader’s objectives and methods are clouded in confusion, daily U-turns and boasts that within hours are revealed to be false. Continue reading...

But the resumed fighting is also likely to push oil prices towards $90 a barrel, potentially taking Trump closer to defeats at the US midterm elections that could bequeath him a final two years as a lame, if angry, duck. In a sign of the strategic chaos, Trump proposed – then almost immediately abandoned – a suggestion that the US could charge tolls for clearing the strait, leaving it unclear if Washington had any vision for the future of the waterway.

Many workable alternatives are available, including models based on the strait of Malacca or the Bosphorus and Dardanelles model, both of which have been discussed by the International Maritime Organization (IMO). Iran and Oman – the two littoral states – are willing to engage on these, but so derelict is the Washington policymaking machinery that the US has no proposal of its own to offer. In briefings on Tuesday, the White House insisted that the 20% US toll first announced by Trump the day before was a serious plan, claiming the president had been considering the proposal for a long time. Hours later, however, the product of Trump’s extensive cogitations was jettisoned after the scale of the revolt from shipping firms, members of his own administration and the region became apparent.

Five months of U-turns and false boasts leave Donald Trump in worse position than when he started

Donald Trump has taken the war with Iran into a new, murkier phase as the two sides move further and further from the vague memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed on 17 June.

And as during the opening phase of the conflict, the US leader’s objectives and methods are clouded in confusion, daily U-turns and boasts that within hours are revealed to be false.

Washington’s short-term aim is clear enough – to regain control of the strait of Hormuz from Iran – and the president seems willing to extend the bombing campaign from beyond Iran’s southern shores to achieve this.

But the resumed fighting is also likely to push oil prices towards $90 a barrel, potentially taking Trump closer to defeats at the US midterm elections that could bequeath him a final two years as a lame, if angry, duck.

In a sign of the strategic chaos, Trump proposed – then almost immediately abandoned – a suggestion that the US could charge tolls for clearing the strait, leaving it unclear if Washington had any vision for the future of the waterway.

Many workable alternatives are available, including models based on the strait of Malacca or the Bosphorus and Dardanelles model, both of which have been discussed by the International Maritime Organization (IMO). Iran and Oman – the two littoral states – are willing to engage on these, but so derelict is the Washington policymaking machinery that the US has no proposal of its own to offer.

In briefings on Tuesday, the White House insisted that the 20% US toll first announced by Trump the day before was a serious plan, claiming the president had been considering the proposal for a long time.

Hours later, however, the product of Trump’s extensive cogitations was jettisoned after the scale of the revolt from shipping firms, members of his own administration and the region became apparent.

That ever such an idea was even proposed is deeply embarrassing, since so many European leaders (and US officials) were on record saying freedom of navigation was a cornerstone of the rules-based order and a pillar of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, had previously argued that tolls were not compatible with international law.

Only last week the 40-strong IMO council – of which the US is an active member – passed a motion reaffirming “that passage through the strait should remain free of any tolls and charges

payload.title: Yhdysvaltain Hormuz-linja horjuu – Trump perui nopeasti 20 prosentin maksuesityksen
payload.summary: Washington pyrkii saamaan Hormuzinsalmen takaisin hallintaansa Iranilta, mutta Yhdysvaltain keinot ja pidemmän aikavälin suunnitelma ovat jääneet epäselviksi.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain pyrkimys saada Hormuzinsalmi takaisin hallintaansa Iranilta ei ole vienyt kiistaa lähemmäs ratkaisua. Presidentti Donald Trump on vienyt Iranin-vastaisen sodan uuteen ja aiempaa epäselvempään vaiheeseen, samalla kun Washington on väläyttänyt pommitusten laajentamista ja perunut nopeasti esityksen salmen avaamiseen liittyvästä 20 prosentin maksusta.

## Kesäkuun yhteisymmärrys etääntyy

Yhdysvallat ja Iran ovat ajautuneet yhä kauemmas 17. kesäkuuta allekirjoitetusta väljästä yhteisymmärrysmuistiosta. Guardianin analyysin mukaan Trumpin tavoitteita ja menetelmiä ovat leimanneet viiden kuukauden ajan päivittäiset suunnanmuutokset sekä julkiset väitteet, jotka ovat osoittautuneet vääriksi jo tuntien kuluessa. Lehden arvion mukaan presidentin asema on nyt heikompi kuin konfliktin alussa.

Washingtonin lyhyen aikavälin tavoite on analyysin mukaan selvä: se pyrkii saamaan Hormuzinsalmen uudelleen hallintaansa Iranilta. Trump vaikuttaa olevan valmis laajentamaan pommituskampanjaa Iranin etelärannikon ulkopuolelle tavoitteen saavuttamiseksi. Tämä ei kuitenkaan vastaa kysymykseen siitä, miten meriväylää olisi määrä hallita pidemmällä aikavälillä.

Taistelujen jatkuminen voi analyysin mukaan nostaa öljyn hinnan kohti 90:tä dollaria barrelilta. Hintakehitys voisi puolestaan heikentää Trumpin poliittista asemaa Yhdysvaltain välivaalien lähestyessä. Mahdolliset vaalitappiot voisivat vähentää hänen toimintakykyään presidenttikautensa kahden viimeisen vuoden aikana.

## Maksusuunnitelma kaatui vastustukseen

Trump esitti maanantaina, että Yhdysvallat voisi periä 20 prosentin maksua salmen raivaamisesta ja avaamisesta. Valkoinen talo vakuutti vielä tiistain tiedotustilaisuuksissa suunnitelman olevan vakavasti otettava ja presidentin harkinneen sitä pitkään. Esitys hylättiin kuitenkin jo tunteja myöhemmin, kun varustamot, Trumpin oman hallinnon jäsenet ja alueen toimijat nousivat sitä vastaan. Nopea perääntyminen lisäsi epäselvyyttä Washingtonin suunnitelmista.

## Vaihtoehtoisia malleja on käsitelty

Hormuzinsalmen järjestelyihin on olemassa Malakansalmen sekä Bosporinsalmen ja Dardanellien käytäntöihin pohjautuvia vaihtoehtoja. Kansainvälinen merenkulkujärjestö IMO on käsitellyt näitä malleja, ja salmen rantavaltiot Iran ja Oman ovat lähteen mukaan valmiita keskustelemaan niistä. Yhdysvalloilla ei silti ole omaa ehdotusta tarjottavana. Neuvottelukelpoisista vaihtoehdoista huolimatta salmen tuleva hallintomalli on avoin, ja osapuolet etääntyvät samalla kesäkuussa kirjatusta yhteisymmärryksestä.

Five months of U-turns and false boasts leave Donald Trump in worse position than when he started

Donald Trump has taken the war with Iran into a new, murkier phase as the two sides move further and further from the vague memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed on 17 June.

And as during the opening phase of the conflict, the US leader’s objectives and methods are clouded in confusion, daily U-turns and boasts that within hours are revealed to be false.

Washington’s short-term aim is clear enough – to regain control of the strait of Hormuz from Iran – and the president seems willing to extend the bombing campaign from beyond Iran’s southern shores to achieve this.

But the resumed fighting is also likely to push oil prices towards $90 a barrel, potentially taking Trump closer to defeats at the US midterm elections that could bequeath him a final two years as a lame, if angry, duck.

In a sign of the strategic chaos, Trump proposed – then almost immediately abandoned – a suggestion that the US could charge tolls for clearing the strait, leaving it unclear if Washington had any vision for the future of the waterway.

Many workable alternatives are available, including models based on the strait of Malacca or the Bosphorus and Dardanelles model, both of which have been discussed by the International Maritime Organization (IMO). Iran and Oman – the two littoral states – are willing to engage on these, but so derelict is the Washington policymaking machinery that the US has no proposal of its own to offer.

In briefings on Tuesday, the White House insisted that the 20% US toll first announced by Trump the day before was a serious plan, claiming the president had been considering the proposal for a long time.

Hours later, however, the product of Trump’s extensive cogitations was jettisoned after the scale of the revolt from shipping firms, members of his own administration and the region became apparent.

That ever such an idea was even proposed is deeply embarrassing, since so many European leaders (and US officials) were on record saying freedom of navigation was a cornerstone of the rules-based order and a pillar of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, had previously argued that tolls were not compatible with international law.
